title: Promptset audit, change-trace, and automated rollback playbook
creator: Sophie Turner
description: Goal: Define and implement an operational playbook + lightweight automation that ties promptset and golden-dataset changes to model/config rollouts and automatically triggers rollback or gated promotions when eval regressions exceed thresholds. Scope covers curator workflows, ACLs, versioning conventions, eval gating rules, observability signals, and runbook steps for on-call and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Every promptset and golden snapshot has an immutable fingerprint and human-friendly changelog linked to the config change that introduced it. 2) Config/model rollouts include a pre-rollout eval against the golden snapshot and a post-rollout eval; regressions above threshold (precision drop >3% or human-score delta >0.08) automatically trigger an annotated rollback candidate and page the PM/owner. 3) RBAC for creating/approving golden snapshots exists: curator -> approver -> signer flow. 4) A public Console playbook view shows last evals, signature, and rollback history for each promptset. 5) Runbook for on-call describes clear steps for triage and safe rollback within 30 minutes.
description_background: Context: We have recurring incidents where small promptset tweaks or default config changes cause subtle regressions detectable only in seeded evals. Current ownership and auditability are vague: curators update sets in Drive, PRs lack fingerprint metadata, and rollout pipelines don't consistently gate on golden-set regressions. This ticket operationalizes an end-to-end flow to reduce these incidents and speed recovery.
proposed_solution: 1) Metadata: add immutable fingerprint (SHA256 of normalized prompt bundle + curator metadata) and require a signer signature for any snapshot promoted to 'golden'. 2) Storage: store golden snapshot metadata in the Prompt Registry (Console backend) with fields: fingerprint, curator, approver, signed_at, release_tag, linked_pr/commit. 3) Eval gating: add pre/post rollout eval stage in CI that runs canonical prompt bundles and compares to baseline; expose a gating API that the rollout pipeline calls. 4) Automation: when post-rollout regression > threshold, create a rollback candidate ticket (automatically populate repro steps, failing cases, linked model/config), annotate deployment and optionally trigger automated rollback if opt-in. 5) UX: Console shows change history, signature badge, and a one-click rollback UI for authorized roles. 6) Security/Compliance: signers must be in the 'golden-approvers' group and actions emit structured audit logs to KMS-protected storage.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - False positives: tightening thresholds may block healthy rollouts; will include an allowlist for low-risk experiments. - Operational overhead: sign-off steps add friction to rapid iteration; mitigate by allowing a canary path with reduced restrictions. - Storage/retention: keeping every snapshot forever increases cost; adopt TTL policy for non-promoted snapshots. - Automation rollback needs clear guardrails to avoid rolling back for noisy metrics; require multi-signal confirmation (eval + human review or secondary metric) unless explicit auto-rollback opt-in is enabled.
milestones: Design metadata fingerprint and signer workflow (doc + API schema)
Console UI: golden snapshot view and signature badge
Backend: Prompt Registry storage and audit log integration
CI: pre/post rollout eval gating and threshold config
Automation: rollback candidate creation + notification plumbing
implementation_notes: - Backend owners: Eng/runtime (for eval runners) and Eng/platform (for registry + audit logs). - Use existing eval harness used by PM-4126 as baseline but extend to capture per-case metadata. - Leverage HMAC signing with KMS for signer attestations; store signer key IDs in registry. - Add 'golden-promote' endpoint that enforces ACL and records signer metadata. - Expose gating verdict via a short-lived signed token consumable by rollout orchestrator.
notes: This ticket is the PM-side orchestration and playbook. Separate engineering tickets will track schema changes, registry migrations, and CI integration. Coordinate with Compliance for retention settings.
